questions.problem:
Given the quartic function $f(x;a,b,c)=a{x}^{4}+b{x}^{3}+c{x}^{2},$ compute ${∇}_{b,c}\,f.$
${∇}_{b,c}\,f=\text{ }$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
To compute ${∇}_{b,c}\,f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to $b$ and $c.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂b} & =\frac{∂}{∂b}(a{x}^{4}+b{x}^{3}+c{x}^{2})={x}^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂c} & =\frac{∂}{∂c}(a{x}^{4}+b{x}^{3}+c{x}^{2})={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{b,c}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂b} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂c}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3} \\ {x}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the function $f(x,y;a,b)=ax+by,$ compute ${∇}_{a,b}\,f.$
${∇}_{a,b}\,f=\text{ }$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
To compute ${∇}_{a,b}\,f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to $a$ and $b.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂a} & =\frac{∂}{∂a}(ax+by)=x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂b} & =\frac{∂}{∂b}(ax+by)=y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{a,b}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂a} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂b}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the function $f(x;w)=2{w}_{1}{x}_{1}-5{w}_{2}{x}_{2},$ compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$ with the input $x={[\begin{aligned}-2,\,8\end{aligned}]}^{T}.$
${∇}_{w}\,f=\text{ }$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
To compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to each component of $w.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{1}}(2{w}_{1}{x}_{1}-5{w}_{2}{x}_{2})=2{x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{2}}(2{w}_{1}{x}_{1}-5{w}_{2}{x}_{2})=-5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, with $x={[\begin{aligned}-2,\,8\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{w}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} \\ -5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -40\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz$, compute ${∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}\,f).$
${∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}f)=\text{ }$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the variable subset gradient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,z}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz) \\ \frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}yz \\ xy\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the second derivatives with respect to $x$ and $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \frac{∂}{∂x}(yz)=0\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂z}(yz)=y \\  & \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}\,f) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂z} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂z∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{z}^{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & y \\ y & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
